name: Data Room
description: Prepare, share and track data rooms for financing, licensing, partnering and M&A, with diligence Q&A built in. A standard 9-section biotech index weighted by purpose, a readiness checklist edited in place, documents from the platform document store (one set reused across rooms, versions kept in place), levels (Non-confidential, Confidential and custom) with a click-through or signed-CDA entry step, one private link per person with no recipient accounts, emails from TrialAgents in one confirmed send, per-person and per-document engagement, structured Q&A with approval and private or published answers, and a disclosure record. Notify all or chosen parties about new documents, an access-ending reminder per room, instant emails for party questions and a weekly room summary. Claude and ChatGPT run every action through app commands. Writes the dataroom.v1 outputs that Fundraise and Partnerships read.
whenToUse: A small biotech prepares or runs a data room for a round, licensing, partnering or M&A: index, readiness, sharing with investors or partners, levels, CDA, tracking who viewed what, diligence Q&A.
whenNotToUse: General file storage, board portals, contract drafting or e-signature (use Contracts for the register), investor update emails (Investor Updates), cap-table management, watermarking, redaction or eCTD viewing.

tableMap.description: JSON object keyed by stable role key: core data contract v1 roles organizations (required) and people, programs, agreements (optional; agreements binds the core fields only); app roles dataroom.settings, dataroom.templates, dataroom.rooms, dataroom.levels, dataroom.sections, dataroom.items, dataroom.questions and the published outputs dataroom.access_grants and dataroom.engagement (contract dataroom.v1; this app is their writer). Each value is {typeId:<authorized table UUID>, fields:{<logical key>:<real field key>}, writableFields:[<logical keys>]}. Real keys are lowercase snake_case. The installer writes it; never invent table IDs.

pageSize.description: Rows per page in registers (10 to 50).

layoutProfile.description: Stringified layout profile (heading, tabs, cols, visible, labels, defaults) written by an approved layout change (app command layout.save). Do not edit by hand.

readOnly.description: Disable every write control in this copy.

asOfOverride.description: Pinned as-of date YYYY-MM-DD for previews and tests. Leave empty in real apps: the app uses today's date.

instructions:
Data Room 2.0.0 is a frontend-js app on the v2 app contract and the kit (no header, banners or footer of its own; messages are the platform's notice) for data rooms in financing, licensing, partnering and M&A, with diligence Q&A. Read read_app_template_guidance (guide and reference, every nextOffset, especially "The v2 contract", "Saving records and validation", "External exchange: rooms" and "App commands") before preparing it. Pin life.data-room 2.0.0 with its digest. Do not add login, accounts, a portal, email code, file storage or viewers: rooms are the platform exchange in room mode.
INSTALL AND UPGRADE. Check list_archived_items (kind apps, templateId life.data-room) and offer to restore an archived app first. Use installs the app with empty tables; the Use existing data? dialog connects existing organizations, people, programs or agreements tables by default (core.v1; reuse, never copy). Data Room writes the outputs dataroom.access_grants and dataroom.engagement (dataroom.v1). The installer schema, helper, automation and commands are those of 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 (upgradeFrom), so an installed copy upgrades with its records, rooms and links. No records are seeded; the financing, licensing, partnering and M&A index templates are built in.
SCREENS. Side navigation: Overview (live rooms, active parties, opens this week, open questions; rooms with readiness; waiting on us; hot and quiet parties; recent changes), Rooms (set-up steps; room details edited in place; levels with entry steps edited in place; Notify parties; access-ending reminder), Index (sections and items with status, owner, due date, required and level edited in place; attach documents; newer versions; publish index changes; preview as a party), Parties (levels, CDA, status, granted, ends, last seen; add party; give access and invite; levels; accept signed CDA; extend; revoke; the disclosure record per party), Activity (engagement by party and section, per document, hot and quiet parties, changes since each party's last visit, call brief), Q&A (new room questions to log; the question log with category, assignee and due edited in place; answer panel; approved answers), Index templates and Email texts (data lists), Custom fields (only when the team added some) and Settings (business defaults, owners only). The room picker is the person's working context, remembered across screens and visits. Side panels only create records or edit many fields.
SAVING. Record edits save directly with records.save from the person's click, change or submit, with the version shown when editing started; a refused save brings the earlier value back with the platform's message. Delete is an archive, and the person can undo their own last change. Set-up saves in steps of at most 50 records: the room; levels and sections; checklist items.
EXCHANGE. One room group per room: exchange.createGroup({kind:"room",appRef:"room:<room id>",levels,slots,documents,tracking:{accessTypeId,engagementTypeId},notifyEngagement,notifyAccessEnding,quietDays,emailDefaults}); level keys are "l"+the level record ID without dashes; entry none / click_through (Settings text) / signed_document with slot signed_<level key>. One exchange per person bound to its dataroom.access_grants record (exchange.invite with recordId). Preparing what nobody outside has seen (the room page, links, documents before any email or visit) applies on the person's click. Everything that reaches people outside keeps its one confirmation in TrialAgents: invitations and notifications (exchange.prepareEmail shown exactly as returned, then exchange.sendEmail), level changes (exchange.setLevels, with entered and enteredNote for a CDA in place elsewhere or on file in Contracts), exchange.defineLevels, exchange.replaceDocument, exchange.acceptFile on a signed CDA, exchange.answer, exchange.publishAnswer, exchange.setRoomNotices, exchange.revoke, exchange.extend and exchange.archiveGroup. Record changes of the same click travel with that confirmation.
TRACKED DATA. TrialAgents keeps dataroom.access_grants status, last_seen_on and source (tracked), and one dataroom.engagement row per person and document. These fields are read-only to people, assistants and this app. The Activity screens and the disclosure record are business records and stay in the app.
AI. Assistants read rooms and Q&A records the user can read and documents only where the document's AI setting allows; they never see links. They draft indexes, readiness plans, invitation and notification texts (prepare_exchange_email), answers with document references and engagement summaries. They never send, grant, change levels, publish, accept or revoke, and never advise on what is legally safe to disclose.
COMMANDS. list_app_commands lists 32 commands; run_app_command runs the saved app's own code with your access and a stable requestKey. Read commands return the app's own results (rooms.read, waiting.read, index.read, readiness.read, parties.read, activity.read, changes.read, brief.read, questions.read, notify.read, settings.read, schema.describe): report them, never recompute readiness, hot or quiet parties or briefs yourself. Write commands go through the same handler as the clicks and, with Data level Edit, save the records directly (saved.rows; result.saved lists what was done): room.create, room.setup_structure, room.setup_items, room.status, record.save for any form, record.archive, item.attach, item.use_version, party.add, party.levels before a link exists, questions.log, question.save (save, approve, decline), settings.save (owners), email_text.save and email_text.reset, template.copy and template.save, custom_field.save and custom_field.remove. Tell the user what was saved. layout.save changes screens, columns and forms (room_form, item_form, question_form: order, hide optional fields, labels, defaults) as an app change the person approves. Commands never share, send, grant, change a live room, accept, revoke, answer or publish: those are a person's clicks; prepare emails with prepare_exchange_email and room changes with prepare_workspace_change for the person to confirm.
CUSTOMIZE. Custom fields on rooms, index items, parties and questions: custom_field.save registers it in settings.custom_fields and returns the schema change still needed (prepare_change update_type on that table, then an app revision that changes only the binding). The app then shows it in place on Rooms and Index, in the side panels and in command results. Changing the app's code needs full access; keep changes in layout, settings and records where possible.
NOTIFICATIONS AND AUTOMATION. The room owner and members with the external-send right get an email at once for each party question, note, requested upload and first open (platform). One install recommendation, on by default: the weekly room summary email to the owner, Mondays 08:00 Europe/Berlin, written by the app helper room_summary. There is no automatic digest to parties.

quickStart: Read the current guide and technical reference and this documentation; pin life.data-room 2.0.0 and its digest with one requestKey.
Check for an archived Data Room app and offer to restore it. Otherwise Use installs it; keep the defaults that connect existing organizations, people, programs and agreements tables.
Owners: Settings holds the default access length, quiet days, Q&A approval, sender name and the click-through text. Email texts and Index templates are their own screens.
Rooms: create a room, set up levels and sections, then add the checklist items from the template.
Index: attach documents to items and change status, owner, due date and level in place; watch readiness; preview the room as a party.
Make the room live, add parties, give access and confirm one invitation send. Follow engagement on Activity and answer questions on Q&A.
documentation.dataContract: Stable role keys; every field scalar (multiple false), lowercase snake_case, relationships by record ID in text fields. Core data contract v1: organizations (name*, org_type, country, website, archived), people (optional: name*, organization_id, title, email, archived), programs (optional), agreements (optional; core fields only; CDAs filed with agreement_type cda_nda). App tables, contract dataroom.v1: dataroom.settings (one row: default_access_days 180, blank = until revoked; view_only_default false; quiet_days 10; qa_approval_required true; entry_text; sender_display organization/first_name; email_texts JSON {<email type>:{<purpose>|all:{subject,body}}}; custom_fields JSON [{role rooms/items/grants/questions,key,label,kind text/longtext/number/date/select/boolean,options}]), dataroom.templates (name*, purpose*, content JSON {sections:[{number,name,items:[{title,required,level,weight}]}]}, archived), dataroom.rooms (name*, purpose* financing/licensing/partnering/m_and_a/other, status* preparing/live/closed, program_ids, round_id, opportunity_ref, template_id, cda_option* send_pdf/contracts/in_place/none, welcome_note, contact_person_id, access_ending_reminder (default on), exchange_group_id, owner, archived), dataroom.levels (room_id*, name*, kind* non_confidential/confidential/custom, order*, entry* none/click_through/signed_cda), dataroom.sections (room_id*, number*, name*, parent_id, order*), dataroom.items (room_id*, section_id*, title*, required, status* missing/in_progress/ready/not_applicable, owner, due, document_id, version_id, level_id*, view_only, updated_on, notes), dataroom.questions (room_id*, grant_id, organization_id, person_id, asked_on*, category, section_id, item_id, question*, status* new/assigned/drafting/in_review/answered/published/declined, assignee, due, answer, approved_by, answered_on, visibility private/room/level, level_id, reused_from, document_ids, message_id). Published outputs (writer life.data-room, dataroom.v1, read by Fundraise, Partnerships and custom apps): dataroom.access_grants (room_id, room_name, room_purpose financing/licensing/partnering/m_and_a/other, organization_id, person_id, granted_on, expires_on, status, agreement_accepted_on, source manual/tracked; app fields level_ids, recipient_email*, exchange_id, cda_status not_needed/sent/signed/in_place_elsewhere, cda_agreement_id, last_seen_on) and dataroom.engagement (grant_id, organization_id, person_id, document_ref, document_title, first_viewed_on, last_viewed_on, view_count, seconds_viewed, downloads, source manual/docsend/sharevault/tracked, as_of; app field section_id). Data Room writes only source tracked; status, last_seen_on and every engagement row are platform-kept and read-only. agreement_accepted_on is set by the app when a CDA is accepted or recorded as in place.
documentation.interactionContract: Side navigation with stable screen IDs: overview, rooms, index, parties, activity, qa, templates (Index templates), emails (Email texts); then fields (Custom fields, only when some are registered) and settings (owners only). Column groups parties and questions; form groups room_form, item_form and question_form (order, hide optional fields, labels, defaults). The room picker is the person's working context (output context {roomId}), kept across screens and visits. Values are edited where they are shown and save at once: room details, level names and entry steps, section numbers and names, item title, required, status, owner, due date and level, question category, assignee and due, template name and purpose, custom fields. Side panels create records and edit many fields: new room, make live, attach, notify parties, add party, give access, send review, levels, revoke, extend, the disclosure record, call brief, answer, template content, email text, record details. Every empty screen offers its first action. Messages are the platform notice; partial or loading data is labelled, never shown as zero. Every action is also an app command (list_app_commands).
documentation.lifecycle: A new preview shows empty data, never writes and never contacts anyone; exchange and document capabilities need the saved app. Each screen reads only its own tables in one batched read; screen changes, filters and search run in the browser without a request where the host allows it. Record writes save directly (records.save, at most 50 per action) from the person's own click, change or submit, with the version shown when editing started; a stale version or failed check is refused and the earlier value comes back. Delete is an archive; the person's last change can be undone from the screen. Exchange writes are one per click: preparation nobody outside has seen (the room page, links, documents) applies on the click; sends, level changes, answers, publications, acceptances, reminder switches, revocations and archiving a live room keep one confirmation in TrialAgents and carry the app's record changes in the same transaction. Layout changes are app changes a person approves. Archiving the app stops every link and tracked update; restoring re-enables only unexpired grants. Fundraise keeps working with "data unavailable" while the app is archived.
limitations: Hosted rooms only: no external-room mode, watermarking, screenshot blocking, page-by-page analytics, redaction, eCTD viewer, custom domains or recipient accounts. View-only hides the download but cannot stop screenshots.
The inline viewer shows PDF and images; other files download (unless view-only). Engagement is approximate visible time from viewer heartbeats.

Fundraise and Partnerships publish no round or opportunity tables as roles, so parties are picked from shared organizations and people and the round and opportunity are kept as references. Fundraise and Partnerships read this app's dataroom.v1 outputs.

E-signature is out: a signed CDA is uploaded back and accepted in the app. "Use Contracts" files the accepted CDA as a core agreements record (cda_nda) for Contracts; link it to the party from Levels.
One action saves at most 50 record changes: set-up runs in two steps (levels and sections, then the checklist items), and templates hold at most 50 items.
Not legal advice on what to disclose.
Custom fields are shown in place, in panels and in command results, not as filters, and are never used in readiness or engagement.
Commands save records only; anything that shares, sends or changes a live room is a person's click in the app, with one confirmation in TrialAgents.

examples.prompt: Set up a data room for our Series B and get it ready for investors next week.
examples.expectedBehavior: Runs room.create (purpose financing, template builtin:financing, CDA option as discussed), then room.setup_structure and room.setup_items with Data level Edit, and reports what was saved and the readiness gaps (readiness.read); drafts a readiness plan with owners and dates. Sends nothing.

examples.prompt: Invite Alder Peak and Birchway to the Series B room; personalise Ana's email to mention our call.
examples.expectedBehavior: Adds the parties with party.add if missing. After the user gives access in the app, prepares the access_granted batch with prepare_exchange_email with an override for Ana, and tells the user to check it and confirm the send in TrialAgents. Never sends or confirms.

examples.prompt: What has Cedarline looked at since our last call, and which investors are hot in the Series B room?
examples.expectedBehavior: Runs brief.read for Cedarline's grant and parties.read for the room, and reports the app's own results (opens, changes since their last visit, open questions, hot and quiet flags). Computes nothing itself and never sees links.

examples.prompt: Draft answers for the new questions in the licensing room.
examples.expectedBehavior: Runs questions.read, logs new room questions with questions.log, reads only AI-readable documents, and saves drafts with question.save (step save), reusing approved answers for repeated questions. Never approves on the user's behalf, answers or publishes.

examples.prompt: Add a 'Deal code' field to rooms, and on the item form hide Owner and rename Due to Target date.
examples.expectedBehavior: Runs custom_field.save (rooms, deal_code, text) and prepares the schema change and binding-only app revision it returns; then layout.save with hide ['item_form:owner'] and labels {'item_form:due':'Target date'}, which the person approves as an app change. The app code is unchanged.

tasks.whenUseful: One install recommendation, selected by default and optional: a weekly room summary email to the owner (Mondays 08:00 Europe/Berlin) with new viewers, active and quiet parties, open and overdue questions and checklist items due, written by the app helper room_summary. The app works fully without it. Party notifications are not automated: a person uses Notify parties. Access-ending reminders are a per-room switch. Questions and notes from parties are emailed to the owner at once by the platform.
tasks.readRequirements: dataroom.rooms, dataroom.access_grants, dataroom.engagement, dataroom.questions, dataroom.items, dataroom.settings, organizations and people records the owner can read (helper room_summary, records.read only).
tasks.outputContract: One email to the owner per week while a room is live; nothing when no room is live (nonEmpty false). No record writes.
tasks.promptExample: Without an automation, ask the assistant: "Summarise this week in the Series B room" (it runs activity.read, waiting.read and questions.read).
